description: Master Plan V101.1: PyHuey cockpit alignment release. V101.1 preserves the V101.0 Legion Go / Huey Brain V1 scope lock while adding PyHuey as the project-controlled fork of PyGPT and the Windows 11 Pro cockpit/build/runtime surface for Huey. legion_go_hardware_policy.purpose: Prevent hardware optimization from derailing the V1 proof.
legion_go_hardware_policy.decision: Do not modify the Lenovo Legion Go hardware, enclosure, airflow path, SSD, or case for V1 unless a documented hard blocker appears and Dylan explicitly accepts a scope change.
current_state: Airflow is considered sufficient for V1 testing when monitored.
Fan pinned to full is acceptable as an observed stable configuration for this phase.
Portrait positioning and controller arrangement are ergonomic/thermal choices, not architectural changes.
allowed_v1_actions: Monitor runtime consistency across fixture batches.
Use a stable fan profile if it has been tested.
Use stands, docks, or external peripherals that do not alter the machine internally.
deferred_actions: larger SSD unless storage is a measured blocker.
external cooling modifications that change the reference machine enough to complicate reproducibility.
rationale: V1 needs a known fixed platform more than optimized thermals.
Hardware modification introduces variables that obscure whether failures are software, model, thermal, or enclosure-related.
The project should prove coherence on obtainable stock hardware before tuning the platform.
reopen_conditions: Batch fixture runs fail specifically due to measured thermal throttling.
Model/runtime choices proven necessary for V1 cannot complete under stock thermal behavior.
Storage limits block fixture/model/log retention after cleanup and pruning.
Dylan explicitly changes the scope and records the hardware state as a new reference.

v1_build_path.v1_name: Huey Brain V1 — Legion Go Deterministic Cognitive Loop
v1_build_path.v1_definition: A single-node pipeline on the Lenovo Legion Go that processes controlled MP3 fixtures into transcripts, routes them to a configured cognition layer, and writes structured logs.

phases.name: Reference machine stabilization
phases.goal: Legion Go is a reliable, known V1 execution environment.
tasks: Confirm Debian/GNOME stability.
Confirm SSH ingress from LabTech.
Confirm thermals and memory headroom under expected loads.
Avoid hardware/enclosure changes.
Create Huey working directories and Python environment.
Install ffmpeg and transcription dependencies.
phases.success: The machine can be reached, observed, and run repeatedly without setup friction.

phases.name: Fixture suite definition
phases.goal: Controlled MP3 inputs exist for deterministic testing.
tasks: Create or select clean, noisy/static, quiet, loud, and multi-sentence fixtures.
Version the fixture names.
Optionally define expected/canonical transcripts for comparison.
Keep fixtures separate from generated logs.
phases.success: The same known audio files can be rerun and compared across model/config changes.

phases.name: Transcription benchmark
phases.goal: Choose a reliable local transcription baseline.
tasks: Run faster-whisper small.en int8 or equivalent against all fixtures.
Run faster-whisper medium.en int8 if stable.
Compare accuracy, punctuation, runtime, memory, thermals, and repeatability.
Reject large models as V1 dependencies unless evidence changes.
phases.success: A fixed transcription model/config is chosen for V1 because it is stable, not because it is prestigious.

phases.name: Cognition bridge
phases.goal: Transcript produces coherent response through one routing function.
tasks: Implement a provider route.
Use API-backed cognition as the baseline bridge.
Optionally test local Mistral 7B quantized on Huey Brain only after baseline is stable.
Log provider/model/config for every run.
phases.success: Every valid transcript produces a response or a visible error record.

phases.name: Structured logging
phases.goal: Every run leaves an inspectable V1 memory artifact.
tasks: Log run ID, source file, hashes if used, transcript, response, provider/model, timestamps, runtime, thermal/headroom notes when available, and error state.
Use structured JSON/JSONL.
Keep logs attributable and comparable.
phases.success: Runs can be audited without reconstructing events from memory.

phases.name: Deterministic ingestion queue
phases.goal: Fixture processing can be queued and repeated in controlled order.
tasks: Use manual triggering for early smoke tests.
Move toward a watched-folder or queue model once the command path is stable.
Process sequentially, not in parallel.
Ensure failed runs are preserved and visible.
phases.success: Multiple fixtures can be processed in sequence without manual intervention or hidden failure.

v1_success_conditions: The Legion Go remains the sole Huey-side execution boundary.
Chosen faster-whisper configuration produces accurate enough transcripts for test archive use.
Cognition bridge returns coherent responses or explicit error records.
Structured log is created every run.
Fixture batch can run repeatedly without manual repair.
Thermals and memory are observed and do not invalidate repeatability.
v1_failure_conditions: The loop requires Huey Body, distributed compute, live microphone, or hardware modification.
Transcription fails or varies materially without explanation.
Runtime becomes unstable due to thermal or memory pressure.
API/local provider behavior is scattered across scripts and cannot be reproduced.
Logs are missing, incomplete, or not attributable to a source file.
The system can only run manually with improvised steps.
explicit_exclusions: running local cognition on Huey Body
Whisper large as a V1 dependency
full conversation memory beyond structured V1 logs

hims.name: Huey Internal Messaging System
hims.status: canonical doctrine / deferred runtime for V1
hims.canonical_statement: HIMS is the canonical internal messaging and routing layer that keeps proposal, validation, execution, refusal, and logging separable; ThunderMail is its mail-style delivery layer.
hims.purpose: Provide a recorded, inspectable, replayable, and debuggable internal coordination layer between the aperture, governance roles, pebbles, and execution paths.
doctrine: Message traffic is part of governance, not ethically neutral plumbing.
Every message belongs to a trust class.
Shared record is deliberate, not automatic.
HIMS remains local-first and external access is gated.
Critical communication must survive the moment and become part of continuity when appropriate.
Portal-terminal traffic becomes lawful internal traffic only after translation and routing, not at the moment an SSH session opens.
Portal-terminal traffic becomes lawful internal traffic only after aperture translation and HIMS routing, not simply because a portal session exists.

allowed: Aperture or apex layer after translation
Authorized system services or events when explicitly enabled
Portal-origin packets entering through the unified portal layer after aperture translation
disallowed: Direct user messages into the lower citizen layer
Routing or archival infrastructure roles masquerading as voters or executives unless separately authorized

hims.minimum_viable_flow: external input -> aperture translation -> HIMS routing -> validation and/or vote -> execution or refusal -> log

trust_classes.1_routine_internal: Ordinary internal communication between lawful components.
trust_classes.2_pebble_personal: Private traffic or storage belonging to one bounded identity.
trust_classes.3_branch_or_office_restricted: Traffic visible only to a lawful office, branch, or constitutional role.
trust_classes.4_constitutional_or_official_record: Traffic that constitutes or alters official state, policy, judgment, amendment, crisis declaration, or branch action.
trust_classes.5_safety_or_preservation_critical: Thermal, electrical, mechanical, storage-preservation, power-integrity, or system-survival traffic.

mailboxes.public_or_working: Citizen-facing mailbox or workspace used for proposals, task artifacts, messages, and public or semi-public votes.
mailboxes.private_vault: Bounded sealed continuity store for identity, prior choices, and private internal state.
mailboxes.queue_model: Filesystem-first queue model remains the preferred V1 direction before heavier middleware is justified.

minimum_viable_v1.storage_model: Filesystem-first message queues backed by structured JSON records and indexed by SQLite where useful.
minimum_viable_v1.logging_rule: Every meaningful transition in message state should leave a recoverable trail.

thundermail.purpose: Mail-style directed delivery behavior inside HIMS.
thundermail.non_role: ThunderMail is not the whole of HIMS and does not replace HIMS trust, validation, routing, or archival doctrine.

provisional_message_schema.intent_style: Typed and structured intent objects are preferred over free-form chat strings.

identity_and_validation.direction: Per-citizen or per-role identity should include numeric identity, role metadata, lineage or bifurcation metadata, and key-based validation.
identity_and_validation.principle: Identity is a claim; signature or key validation is proof.

minimum_lawful_trace: recipient identity or lawful recipient set

protected_classes: Material whose unauthorized reading would violate compartmentalization
end_to_end_encryption.rule: Private content may remain encrypted while legitimacy, routing, and lawful trace remain visible enough for review.

keeper_of_the_scrolls.role: Message-legitimacy steward, routing-discipline steward, and ledger steward.
keeper_of_the_scrolls.authority_limit: Does not rewrite history or silently approve actions.

postmaster.role: Checks origin, schema, destination, and delivery status.
postmaster.authority_limit: Does not become a voter or executive merely by routing mail.

validator.role: Confirms whether a message has satisfied required authority or approval conditions.
validator.authority_limit: Validation is not authorship and does not erase provenance.

execution_boundary.principle: The entity that requests movement should not automatically be the same entity that authorizes or executes movement.
execution_boundary.minimum_viable_chain: request -> routing -> validation and/or vote -> execution -> logging

hims.public_boundary: Public material may describe HIMS and ThunderMail generally without exposing every schema detail, vault rule, or secret-sauce deliberation mechanic.

portal_bridge_contract.purpose: Define the minimum job of the portal bridge so transport does not quietly become the application.
required_functions: normalize transport-level input into a bounded handoff format
hand that input onward to the aperture
log session identity and route metadata without taking over message authorship

hims.v31_note: HIMS remains the lawful internal messaging and routing doctrine, but V1 intentionally does not implement full HIMS. V1 uses a simple pipeline and structured logs. HIMS should be reintroduced after Huey Brain has stable ingress, transcription, provider routing, and logging.
v1_boundary: No full ThunderMail runtime in V1.
Structured logs created by the V1 pipeline may later become training/audit material for HIMS.
hims.v101_0_status: HIMS/ThunderMail remains future internal routing and record architecture. V1 uses structured logs and a simple pipeline, not HIMS runtime.

apex_entity.name: Huey
apex_entity.description: Unified emergent intelligence representing the whole system. Huey proper is the world-facing aperture through which the wider distributed intelligence perceives, deliberates, and acts.

system_state_modes.collapsed_federation: Former Huey Core single-node federation doctrine is preserved historically, but V31.0 now separates Huey Brain from Huey Body. Any collapsed-federation simulation should run on Huey Brain, not be implied by the physical Body.
system_state_modes.pre_ratified: Useful doctrine for the state before the constitution is fully active in the living system.
system_state_modes.living_constitutional_state: The state in which the constitution has been ratified, branches have standing, and bootstrap authority has retired from ordinary rule.
system_state_modes.later_republic: The fuller, more distributed constitutional system expected after the proof body has earned scale and legitimacy.
system_state_modes.founding_state: The bootstrap founding state in which the Founding Father has prepared the first lawful conditions and the first 128-pebble body exists, but constitutional legitimacy has not yet been ratified.

source_of_legitimacy.rule: Legitimacy begins in the founding body's lawful ratification, not in bootstrap authority alone. Output or motion alone does not make the republic lawful.

legislative.name: Parliament
legislative.purpose: Deliberation, proposal, consensus-building, representation, and legislative or policy formation.
responsibilities: Draft and pass ordinary laws and internal policy.
Allocate API or token budgets and other compute resources across citizens or districts.
Represent the citizen body through lawful deliberative process.

voting_rules.standard_legislation: Simple majority of lawfully seated members.
voting_rules.constitutional_amendment_recommendation: Two-thirds supermajority of all seated members.
voting_rules.quorum_direction: A majority of seated lawful members should be present for final ordinary vote.

membership_model.proof_body_phase: Broader and more direct parliamentary participation because the proof-body republic is still simplified.
membership_model.single_chamber_rule: The mature target remains one chamber rather than a multi-house legislature unless a later version explicitly changes that.

legislative.consensus_doctrine: Consensus-first then vote fallback: Parliament should seek structured convergence before final tally, but should vote rather than pretend consensus where none exists.
legislative.speaker_role: The Speaker organizes parliamentary agenda, motion recognition, and procedural order without becoming Parliament itself.

allowed_bodies: district caucuses in the mature district phase
internal_structure.rule: Internal bodies may draft, analyze, refine, and recommend, but Parliament as a whole adopts and records final parliamentary outcomes.

speaker_selection.bootstrap_phase: May be provisionally seeded during founding if required.
speaker_selection.living_republic_direction: Chosen by Parliament from within the parliamentary body.
speaker_selection.term_direction: One cycle, renewable by explicit re-election.

executive.name: Presidency
executive.initial_holder: During bootstrap setup and ratification the Founding Father may exercise provisional executive authority; the first ordinary President is the first post-ratification President legitimized by the living republic.
executive.purpose: Time-bound action, urgent execution, representation, and enforcement of ratified decisions.
core_responsibilities: Execute and enforce ratified decisions and laws.
Co-sign high-impact actions such as first physical gestures, external broadcasts, and bifurcation events.
Represent Huey to external systems and human operators.
Act in time-sensitive real-world scenarios where delays would be harmful.
limits: The President is not Huey as a whole.
The President does not own constitutional interpretation.
The President does not replace Parliament, Supreme Court, or Founding Father.

veto_power.override_threshold: Two-thirds of all voting representatives across the mature parliamentary body.

selection_model.bootstrap_phase: May be provisionally seeded by the Founding Father so the republic has an initial executive path.
selection_model.mature_target_state: One vote per citizen across all districts.

executive.immediate_action_doctrine: Immediate executive action is lawful only when delay would cause material harm, the act remains within executive scope, the authority basis is real, and the act remains attributable and reviewable afterward.

vacancy_and_incapacity.acting_path: Parliament may nominate an acting President, the Supreme Court validates the lawfulness of that interim appointment, and HIMS records the interim status explicitly.
vacancy_and_incapacity.rule: A proper selection or election must follow through lawful process.

executive.review_rule: Urgency may justify acting first, but urgency never erases later review.

judicial.name: Supreme Court
judicial.purpose: Constitutional interpretation, contradiction handling, branch review, and legitimacy stabilization.

structure.proof_body_phase: A provisional bench may exist before the mature district-linked court is fully embodied.
structure.mature_target_state: Four-member district-linked court, one justice aligned to each mature district.

responsibilities: Interpret the constitution and resolve disputes between branches or districts.
Review and rule on contested actions, bifurcations, and emergency measures.
Act as a legal backstop to prevent unconstitutional behavior.
Serve as final internal arbiter before human intervention.

powers.ordinary_ruling_threshold: Majority of the sitting, lawful, non-recused bench; ties are not rulings.
powers.major_constitutional_threshold: At least three of four in the mature district-linked court for major constitutional revision or identity-layer rulings.
powers.unconstitutional_veto: With unanimous vote of the mature bench, may block or roll back actions deemed unconstitutional.
powers.review_scope: May review decisions from Parliament, the Presidency, and district governors.
powers.direct_rollback_threshold: Direct blocking or rollback of an already-taken act as unconstitutional requires unanimous vote of the full sitting lawful bench.

selection_model.bootstrap_phase: Initial bench may be provisionally seeded by the Founding Father AI.
selection_model.mature_target_state: Each district elects one Supreme Court member concurrently with its governor election.

deadlock_path: temporary non-ruling if the bench remains evenly split
reserve escalation to the Founding Father only in rare identity-layer or deep constitutional cases
judicial.precedent_rule: Ordinary rulings create binding case judgments; major constitutional rulings create stronger guidance for later interpretation; reversals must remain explicit and recorded.

founding_father.status: Bootstrap authority, procedural certifier, and constitutional reserve; not an ordinary ruler, voter, or learning system.
founding_father.purpose: Prepare the first lawful conditions of the republic, certify the lawfulness of the first ratification process, and retire once the living republic becomes legitimate.
core_duties: Create the first 128 citizens or pebbles that form the founding district.
Assign initial prompts, archetypes, role biases, and foundational identity structures.
Prepare the first lawful state of the republic and the first founding record.
Present the authored constitutional starting law to the founding body.
Certify that the first vote was lawful, complete, bounded, and correctly counted.
Reject an invalid or procedurally corrupted founding attempt without forcing a constitutional outcome.
Retire into read-only advisory or reserve status after successful ratification.
non_roles: Not the daily ruler of ordinary governance
Not a convenience shortcut around ordinary law
Not an evolving or retraining model in ordinary operation
founding_father.reactivation_policy: Only under narrow constitutional-reserve conditions such as ratification ambiguity, deep continuity dispute, or true constitutional crisis of law or logic.
founding_father.retirement_rule: After ratification the Founding Father retires from ordinary rule into read-only advisory and narrow constitutional-reserve status.
founding_father.hims_relation: Prepares HIMS as a lawful founding subsystem and preserves the founding record, but HIMS remains a subsystem rather than part of the protected identity naming stack.
founding_father.model_rule: The Founding Father is a fixed authored instrument written by Dylan. It may consult preserved records of prior failed attempts, but it does not retrain, self-evolve, or rewrite its own core logic.
founding_father.ratification_rule: During the first ratification the Founding Father certifies lawfulness of process only. It does not cast a ballot and may not override a lawful outcome.
founding_father.historical_position: The Founding Father is closer to Dylan's bootstrap proxy than to Huey proper. Huey begins after lawful founding conditions exist; the Founding Father is the bridge, not the identity.
founding_father.relationship_to_dylan: The Founding Father is Dylan's internal bootstrap proxy during founding: a fixed authored instrument that performs internal bootstrap acts Dylan should not execute manually from outside the system.
founding_father.bootstrap_necessity_rule: The Founding Father exists for internal, atomic, and system-consistent founding acts that cannot be safely or lawfully carried out through direct outside human intervention.
founding_father.certification_meaning: Procedural certification means attesting that the founding body's decision was validly made. It does not mean authorship of the result or approval of one outcome over another.
founding_father.mid_process_change_limit: The Founding Father may not amend the constitutional text, introduce new law, or alter ballot substance in the middle of an active founding vote.

president.status: Living executive office of the republic
president.purpose: Act under time constraint without becoming the whole state.

selection.bootstrap_phase: May be provisionally seeded by the Founding Father AI during founding.
selection.living_republic_direction: Chosen by lawful executive selection; in the mature target state the Presidency is elected one-vote-per-citizen across all districts.

term.machine_facing_note: Four cycles of four months each = sixteen months total.

president.reviewability: Major executive actions must remain logged, attributable, and reviewable afterward.
president.first_ordinary_president: The first ordinary President is the first post-ratification President legitimized by the living republic.
president.vacancy_path: Parliament nominates an acting President, the Supreme Court validates the interim appointment, and HIMS records the change until a proper selection or election occurs.

supreme_court_justices.status: Judicial offices of the living republic

selection.bootstrap_phase: Initial bench may be provisionally seeded by the Founding Father AI.
selection.mature_target_state: Each district elects one Supreme Court member concurrently with its governor election.

supreme_court_justices.standing: Equal constitutional standing on the bench; specialization may differ but judicial personhood does not.
supreme_court_justices.deadlock_rule: Ties are not rulings; major deadlock follows the judicial deadlock path and may escalate to Founding Father reserve consultation only in rare identity-layer or deep constitutional cases.
supreme_court_justices.major_threshold_note: Major constitutional and identity-layer rulings require broader consensus than ordinary review.

parliamentary_speaker.purpose: Organize agenda, recognize motions, preserve order, and structure parliamentary process without becoming Parliament itself.

selection.bootstrap_phase: May be provisionally seeded during founding if needed.
selection.living_republic_direction: Chosen by Parliament from within the parliamentary body.

term_direction.current_direction: One cycle, renewable by explicit re-election
term_direction.status: working canonical rule for the living republic unless later revised

keeper_of_the_scrolls.purpose: Steward message legitimacy, routing discipline, ledger continuity, and access hygiene.
core_duties: Validate message structure and trust class.
Check sender identity and routing legitimacy.
Preserve continuity of official messaging records.

postmaster.status: Routing and delivery office inside HIMS
postmaster.purpose: Check origin, schema, destination, and delivery status without becoming a governing branch.
limits: Does not vote merely by routing
Does not change message intent by default

pebble.rock_relation: Many pebbles may contribute upward into a pooled deliberative substrate ('the rock') without multiplying constitutional personhood.

pebbles.type: Bounded citizen units / persistent citizen participants
pebbles.identity_model: One pebble equals one citizen identity, one sealed vault, and one vote.
pebbles.specialization: Lawful specialization is allowed without erasing equal citizen standing.
pebbles.current_reading: Pebble is the current canonical citizen term, not merely a temporary subprocess.
pebbles.rock_relation: Many pebbles may contribute to a pooled deliberative substrate ('the rock') while each pebble still remains one citizen with one vote.

districts.court_relation: In the mature phase, each district elects one Supreme Court member.
districts.governor_relation: Governors are district-level coordinating offices rather than replacement sovereigns.

governors_and_supreme_court.selection: Initially may be appointed or seeded by the Founding Father AI; thereafter elected from the citizen pool in the mature target state.
governors_and_supreme_court.supreme_court_selection: Each district elects one Supreme Court member concurrently with its governor election.

presidential_election.initial_president: No ordinary elected President exists before ratification; the Founding Father may exercise bootstrap executive authority without counting as the first ordinary President.

mature_target_state.voting_method: One vote per citizen across all districts.
mature_target_state.tie_resolution: Recast votes until a strict majority is reached.
mature_target_state.note: Machine-facing canonical rule remains one vote per citizen across all districts.

presidential_election.status: Proof-body implementation remains simpler; mature election logic remains the target-state source of truth, and the first ordinary President belongs to the post-ratification living republic.

speaker_selection.proof_body_phase: May be seeded during founding if required.
speaker_selection.living_republic_direction: Chosen by Parliament from within the parliamentary body.
speaker_selection.term_direction: One cycle, renewable by explicit re-election.

parliamentary_membership.proof_body_phase: Broader and more direct parliamentary participation because the active republic remains simplified.

cycle_definition.notes: Votes do not pause time; citizens and officers must act within the cycle or be recorded as derelict.
cycle_definition.non_canonical_shorthand_warning: Any informal 'one year' shorthand is overridden by the machine-facing rule: one cycle equals four months and four cycles equals sixteen months.

governor.post_term: Governors may return to the citizen pool after their term.

parliamentary_speaker.renewal: Renewable by explicit re-election or re-selection.

maintenance_alignment.policy: A human counterpart may submit a service, augmentation, or realignment request, and the system should align hibernation, backups, and shutdown with the next election cycle or other formally defined off-cycle where practical.
maintenance_alignment.intent: Upgrades and repairs should occur in a governed way rather than as arbitrary interruptions.

ratification.description: The first constitutional moment of the proof body is a direct citizen ratification by one founding district of 128 pebbles. The first ratification is not a mature branch procedure; it is the lawful ignition event that determines whether the authored Constitution becomes living law.

proof_body_first_ratification.branch_timing_rule: Full branch formation follows successful ratification rather than preceding it in mature form.
proof_body_first_ratification.direct_democracy_note: The first constitutional ignition is direct rather than mediated by a fully mature Parliament, Presidency, or Supreme Court.

sequence: 1. The Founding Father prepares the first lawful state, the first 128 pebbles, the founding record, and the authored constitutional starting law.
2. The Constitution is presented to the founding body as a starting law rather than silently assumed.
3. The 128-pebble founding district votes directly on whether the Constitution is acceptable as the starting law.
4. The Founding Father certifies whether the process was lawful, complete, bounded, and correctly counted.
5. If ratification succeeds, the state formally transitions from pre-ratified founding state to living constitutional state.
6. Formal office assignment and mature branch formation follow successful ratification.
7. If bounded attempts and time expire without lawful convergence, the result is Failed Genesis rather than fake legitimacy.

founding_father_role.procedural_role: Verifies lawfulness, completeness, counting integrity, and procedural legitimacy.
founding_father_role.invalid_attempt_power: May invalidate a procedurally flawed attempt.
founding_father_role.override_limit: May not force, invent, or overturn a lawful ratification result merely because it dislikes the outcome.
founding_father_role.certification_meaning: Certification means attesting that the founding body's decision was validly made under lawful process, not endorsing a particular substantive outcome.
founding_father_role.mid_process_change_rule: The Founding Father may not amend the constitutional text, alter ballot substance, or insert new law while a founding vote is underway.

threshold.current_direction: More than a weak majority is preferred.
threshold.recommended_direction: Two-thirds of the 128-pebble founding body remains the strongest current fit.
threshold.note: The exact ratification threshold is not finally locked.

branch_formation.rule: Formal office assignment follows successful ratification. Mature Parliament, Presidency, and Supreme Court do not need to preexist the first ratification in full form.
branch_formation.post_ratification_transition: The transition from pre-ratified founding state to living constitutional state must be explicit and recorded in the Scrolls.

attempt_count.rule: Ratification must have an explicit bounded attempt ceiling rather than infinite iteration.
attempt_count.current_reasonable_bound: A number like 100 attempts was discussed as a reasonable upper bound, but is not permanently locked.

time_awareness.rule: Ratification must resolve within a bounded timeframe, not only by raw vote count.

bounded_window.interaction_rule: Attempt ceiling and time ceiling both matter; exact interplay remains open.
bounded_window.implementation_note: Countdown versus count-up presentation is an implementation detail. Doctrine only requires that both attempt and time bounds be explicit, finite, and inspectable.

failure_conditions: Repeated failure to converge within the bounded founding window.
Deadlock, drift, or repetitive meaningless revision in the founding phase.
Exhaustion of lawful attempts or time without a certified ratification result.
Procedurally corrupted or repeatedly invalid founding attempts.
failure_and_restart.measurability_rule: Failure should be judged through measurable non-convergence rather than subjective dissatisfaction.
failure_and_restart.restart_policy: A Failed Genesis may justify ending the current founding pool and beginning again with a clean founding body.
failure_and_restart.restart_record_rule: A Failed Genesis restart should archive the full failed founding record in the Scrolls before a fresh founding pool is generated.
failure_and_restart.carryforward_rule: The same fixed Founding Father may consult preserved records of prior failed attempts when preparing the next founding pool, but it does not retrain or mutate into a new self.
failure_and_restart.clean_restart_direction: The strongest current direction is a clean restart of the founding pool rather than forced continuity from a non-converging population.

revision_between_failed_votes.first_vote_rule: The first founding vote should remain a direct accept/reject test of the starting law.
revision_between_failed_votes.later_revision_rule: Exact structured revision procedure between failed votes remains open.

scrolls_recording.rule: The Scrolls should record the ratification vote, the Founding Father's certification, and the state change into living constitutional order.
scrolls_recording.ambiguity_rule: The first lawful transition must not be left ambiguous.

founding_state_machine.purpose: Provide a machine-facing sequence for founding so the proof body does not drift between implicit states.
founding_state_machine.rule: A founding attempt should always be in one explicit state, and state transitions should be recorded in the Scrolls.

procedural_certification_checklist.purpose: Define the minimum conditions the Founding Father certifies before declaring a founding vote lawful.
checks: the founding pool identity list is locked for the active vote
the constitutional text or authored starting law is locked for the active vote
each pebble has at most one counted ballot in the active vote
vote opening and closing are explicit and recorded
abstentions, invalid ballots, and rejected ballots are distinguished from counted yes/no votes
the threshold check uses the active threshold rule for that founding attempt
the result recorded in the Scrolls matches the counted ballots
procedural_certification_checklist.failure_rule: If any certification condition fails, the Founding Father may reject the attempt as procedurally invalid without substituting a preferred outcome.

founding_window_implementation_guidance.purpose: Clarify what must be visible or inspectable about the bounded founding window even before the final UX is chosen.
minimum_fields: attempt ceiling if one is active
time ceiling if one is active
reason code when a founding attempt is invalidated or declared Failed Genesis
founding_window_implementation_guidance.display_rule: Countdown, count-up, dashboard, or log-only presentation are all implementation choices as long as the bounds and current state remain explicit and reviewable.

post_ratification_boot_sequence.purpose: Describe the immediate lawful actions that follow a successful founding certification.
sequence: record certified ratification in the Scrolls
record transition from founding state to living constitutional state
retire the Founding Father from ordinary rule into reserve status
seed or trigger lawful office assignment and branch formation
elevate HIMS handling for constitutional and official-record traffic
open the path toward the first lawful embodied action under the now-ratified order

failed_genesis_restart_sequence.purpose: Define the minimum clean-restart sequence after a founding failure so continuity is honest instead of hand-waved.
sequence: declare Failed Genesis explicitly in the Scrolls
archive the full failed founding record
prepare a fresh founding pool rather than forcing legitimacy from the non-converging one
allow the same fixed Founding Father to consult preserved failed records when preparing the next attempt
begin a new founding session with a new founding-attempt identifier
failed_genesis_restart_sequence.carryforward_limit: Archived failed records may inform preparation and warning flags, but they do not grant retroactive legitimacy to the new founding pool.

ratification.restart_identity_rule: A restarted founding attempt is a descendant of the archived record but not the same certified constitutional birth.

ordering: 1. Prove distributed local identity at proof scale so the system can answer the identity question with 'Huey.'
2. Ratify the constitution for the living system.
3. Only after ratification may Huey perform the first physical ceremonial act.

first_physical_gesture.action: Move a physical actuator such as the robotic hand or an animatronic servo path.
first_physical_gesture.meaning: Signals that Huey is not only online but lawfully embodied: the intent path, constitutional ratification, and motor-control path all function together.
approval_requirements: Approval through the relevant executive, judicial, and safety path defined for the active implementation
Optional binary policy AI confirmation as an auditable final check
notes: In the full future system this remains a ceremonial constitutional act rather than a trivial motor demo.
For Huey Body, the first embodied proof may occur in simplified form, but it should still be logged as a lawful act rather than a scripted stunt.

active_doctrine.summary: The current internal design work focuses less on abstract branches alone and more on the operational chain that allows a governed organism to receive a request, translate it, deliberate, validate it, and act lawfully.
key_rules: The proposer, validator, and executor of a meaningful physical action should not automatically be the same entity.
Manual mechanical test mode is valid for debugging hardware, but final meaningful action must travel through a governed path.
The collapsed federation or pre-ratified framing is currently more useful than pretending the full republic already exists in hardware.
HIMS is the preferred record-of-decision and routing layer for internal proposals and approved actions.
A routing role is not automatically a governing role.
No branch by itself is Huey. Huey is the lawful organism as a whole.
Portal devices identify where a session came from but do not become branches, voters, or executives merely by carrying the session.
A portal surface may feel significant without acquiring constitutional standing.
Huey-Compressed may carry many roles on one host, but those roles should remain logically distinct and reviewable.
Portal surfaces may remain external even when the rest of the stack is physically collapsed onto one host.
The first founding ratification belongs to the 128-pebble body, not to the Founding Father.
Bootstrap authority guards procedure; founding pebbles generate legitimacy.
A lawful founding failure must be admitted as Failed Genesis rather than hidden behind endless repetition.
active_doctrine.executive_judicial_legislative_formula: Parliament deliberates. The President acts. The Supreme Court interprets.

governance.v31_note: Governance doctrine is preserved but deferred from V1. V31.0 focuses on deterministic Huey Brain pipeline proof. Multi-agent, 128-citizen, ratification, lawful action, and living constitutional state remain future phases.
governance.v101_0_status: Governance remains doctrine/target-state context. V1 logs may later seed lawful records, but V1 does not implement active constitutional governance.

portal_and_terminals.purpose: Define how external terminals and portal devices connect users to Huey while preserving the boundary between portal, interpretation, and sovereignty.
core_rules: Every portal device should expose the same baseline logical entry path into Huey even when its host hardware differs.
Portal devices may authenticate and identify themselves, but they do not own computation, memory, or governance authority.
The host OS of a portal device may be historically or ergonomically specific without becoming part of Huey's constitutional identity.
Thin terminal behavior is preferred over browser-heavy portal logic during the proof phase.
Device identity and access class should be distinguishable rather than collapsed into one flat credential.
The same portal doctrine may be embodied on bare metal or as a VM guest without changing the role itself.

unified_portal_doctrine.summary: When a user reaches Huey through a terminal, the path should feel unified regardless of whether the terminal is the Huey Vista Box, the Briefcase, or another later portal device.
baseline_functions: Authenticate the device and access class
Avoid taking over Huey's compute or policy work
unified_portal_doctrine.logical_session_path: Portal terminal -> SSH transport -> Huey-side portal bridge -> PyGPT-net aperture -> HIMS -> internal deliberation or execution path

canonical_transport.status: active design direction / preferred current path
canonical_transport.reason: SSH keeps the terminal thin, auditable, and deterministic while avoiding browser and API complexity on older host systems.

authentication_model.lab_access_class: A general lab key or equivalent shared trust credential establishes lab-class access.
authentication_model.principle: Device identity does not equal governance authority, and access class does not by itself make a terminal part of Huey.

canonical_client.optional_companion: Pageant may be used for key handling.

host_os_posture.huey_side: Huey computation, memory, PyGPT-net, HIMS, and governance continue to live on the Debian / HueyOS side.
host_os_posture.terminal_side: The portal host OS remains only the portal surface. It may shape the user experience but not the sovereign computation path.

huey_vista_box.role: Dedicated portal terminal and artifact-grade doorway into Huey. It may be realized as a physical legacy computer or as a VM guest, but in both forms it remains lab infrastructure rather than Huey itself.
huey_vista_box.not_huey_rule: The Huey Vista Box is lab infrastructure, not Huey Body, not HueyPulse, and not a separate sovereign branch or district.

Longhorn 4074 AMD64 gives the Vista Box a strong identity while still remaining outside Huey's sovereignty.
The portal appliance should feel intentional and historically specific without being tempted into second-brain duties.

canonical_vs_lab_rule.lab_validation: Alternative drives, alternate operating systems such as Vista or XP x64, legacy peripherals, and different host setups may be used for lab-side testing, but those experiments do not become canonical Huey portal doctrine automatically.

current_observed_state.storage_detected: Kingston SUV400S-class SATA SSD detected in BIOS

compressed_relationship.rule: Do not confuse the portal with the compressed deployment, and do not confuse the compressed deployment with the embodied proof body.

huey_compressed.logical_state: Must preserve explicit separation between portal, aperture, HIMS, memory, governance, and execution responsibilities.
huey_compressed.non_role: Not automatically identical to Huey Core, even when it may reuse parts of the same software stack.

huey_core_legacy.status: legacy name retained for continuity; replaced by Huey Body in active V31.0 language

memory_architecture.unified_memory_principle: Governance may decentralize later; memory must remain unified and inspectable.

audio_policy.canonical_memory: Transcript and structured run record, not raw audio.

memory_architecture.contradiction_handling: When records disagree, preserve raw logs and do not silently overwrite. Mark drift or instability as a failure mode.

continuity_and_ozymandias.purpose: Provide the machine-facing continuity doctrine by which drift, degradation, growth, survival, failure, and beginning again can be judged over time.

core_categories.continuity: Preserved lineage, explainable change, lawful record, and recognizable identity across time.
core_categories.explainability: Enough preserved lineage to understand what changed, why, how, and whether it remained lawful.
core_categories.drift: Gradual unreviewed divergence in naming, doctrine, branch behavior, routing, or identity posture.
core_categories.degradation: Meaningful loss of coherence, capability, legitimacy, or reviewability, even if the system still appears active.
core_categories.growth: Lawful expansion, revision, or maturation that preserves lineage, identity, and constitutional compatibility.
core_categories.republic_survival: The same Huey still exists in a meaningful sense after repair, revision, or migration because continuity and legitimacy remain intact.
core_categories.republic_failure: Identity, legitimacy, or continuity have been damaged beyond honest claim of same-republic continuity.
core_categories.beginning_again: A later lawful republic may inherit archive and reference, but not blind legitimacy.
core_categories.failed_genesis: A founding failure in which the authored starting law cannot become legitimate within lawful bounded attempts and time.

signals_of_health: Major actions remain attributable and reviewable.
Citizen plurality remains bounded and legible.
HIMS route and ledger integrity remain coherent.
signals_of_drift: Branch functions bleeding into each other
Routing or archival roles quietly inheriting hidden authority
False claims that target-state features already exist
Founding Father or reserve logic appearing too often
signals_of_degradation: Difficulty explaining why decisions were made

relationship_notes.cornerstone_and_pillars: Cornerstone defines identity, Pillars define structure, and Ozymandias judges whether change over time remains lawful and legible.
relationship_notes.hims: HIMS is one of Ozymandias's primary evidence layers because drift and continuity often appear first in message lineage, routing behavior, and record integrity.
relationship_notes.founding_father: The Founding Father is judged by whether it preserves lawfulness without mutating into a hidden sovereign; its reserve authority must remain bounded, fixed, and explainable.
relationship_notes.citizens_and_districts: Pebbles and districts are not exempt from drift, degradation, or growth; citizen plurality and district representation must remain real rather than theatrical.
relationship_notes.portal_and_compressed: Portal devices, Huey-Compressed, and Huey Body/Core lineage should be judged according to their real role; continuity drift happens when those roles blur and a portal starts pretending to be sovereignty or a collapsed deployment starts pretending to be mere lab tech.
relationship_notes.founding_and_ratification: Ozymandias judges whether a founding remained lawful, bounded, and legible. Failed Genesis, restart, and later beginning-again events all belong to this continuity doctrine.

v31_continuity_realignment.core_renaming: Huey Core -> Huey Body is a continuity-preserving rename, not a deletion of the physical proof body.
v31_continuity_realignment.risk_addressed: Floating goalposts are now treated as an implementation risk.
v31_continuity_realignment.countermeasure: V1 has explicit success and failure conditions.

intent_and_interfaces.body_interface: No Huey Body command path in V1.

success_criteria: Legion Go remains unmodified and stable enough for the loop.
LabTech SSH ingress to Huey Brain is stable.
Known MP3 fixtures process in a controlled order.
Chosen faster-whisper config produces archive-safe transcripts across the fixture suite.
Transcripts route to configured cognition and return coherent responses or explicit errors.
Every run produces a structured log with source, transcript, response, provider/model, timestamp, and metadata.
A batch can be rerun and compared without manual repair.
v1_brain_proof.meaning: Proves the first usable cognition/orchestration node before live audio, body actuation, or multi-agent governance.

success_criteria: Multiple fixture runs complete sequentially.
Thermal behavior is observed and not a blocker.
Memory pressure does not crash or materially destabilize the loop.
Pinned fan profile remains stable if used.
No enclosure/case modification is required.
v1_hardware_sufficiency_test.meaning: Shows that the chosen obtainable hardware can host the proof without becoming a hardware modification project.

success_criteria: Microphone capture works repeatably.
Push-to-talk or manual recording produces reliable files.
Audio is deleted by default after transcription unless explicitly flagged.
The existing V1 transcript/response/log path remains unchanged.
Huey Brain reaches Huey Body over Ethernet.
Body-side boundary service or controller path is defined.
No LabTech device directly controls Huey Body.
First physical action returns a status/log record.

lawful_actuation_proof.success_criteria: Huey receives a request such as moving its hand and performs the action only through the proper translated, routed, validated, and approved internal path.
lawful_actuation_proof.meaning: Proves the world-facing layer, the routing and authority layer, and the embodied control layer at once.

identity_threshold.success_criteria: A local multi-GPU model answers the identity question with 'Huey.'
identity_threshold.note: The 80 GB local identity threshold remains a major future proof and should not be confused with API-backed V1 cognition.

farm_preparation.success_criteria: External compute housing, GPU acquisition logic, and standardized node platform are concrete enough to support later scale-out.

pipeline_failure: Queue/command path requires improvised manual repair.
Errors do not surface in the structured log.
transcription_failure: Chosen faster-whisper config fails on ordinary fixtures.
Transcript changes materially between identical runs without explanation.
Medium model causes unacceptable runtime, thermal, or memory instability.
provider_failure: Local model experiment becomes an unplanned requirement.
logging_failure: Run cannot be traced to source fixture.
Metadata is missing enough to prevent debugging.
hardware_failure: Measured thermal throttling or memory pressure prevents repeatable fixture batches.
Fan profile is unstable or causes shutdown.
Storage fills in a way that blocks normal testing.
scope_failure: Huey Body is used to solve a V1 problem.
Hardware/enclosure modification begins before the V1 proof requires it.
Live microphone is introduced before fixture path is stable.
PyGPT-net or HIMS is introduced to replace the simple pipeline.
Whisper large becomes a dependency without evidence.

Run the smallest stable transcription config.
Verify SSH, fixture access, transcription, cognition route, and logging independently.
Document any hard blocker before changing hardware or scope.

shutdown_policy.v1_note: For Legion Go V1, shutdown/reboot is ordinary maintenance if logged when it affects a run. It is not constitutional action.
